title: Worlds unity, finitude, beginning; against eternity of the world
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): For time stands as ye measure belonging toward ye motion belonging toward creatures. The world was created in time, or with time, not in a pre-existing time. John 17:5. Psalm 90:2; Those who invent an eternal world with Aristotle oppose Scripture — Genesis 1:1; it has a beginning belonging toward time, it stands as not eternal. finite, not infinite; The world stands as one, not many;
pass_b_english: The world is one, not many; finite, not infinite; it has a beginning of time, it is not eternal. Those who invent an eternal world with Aristotle oppose Scripture — Genesis 1:1; Psalm 90:2; John 17:5.
The world was created in time, or with time, not in a pre-existing time. For time is the measure of the motion of creatures.
source_text: Mundus est unus, non plures; finitus, non infinitus; habet principium temporis, non est aeternus. Qui mundum aeternum fingunt cum Aristotele, Scripturae adversantur — Gen. I.1; Psal. XC.2; Joh. XVII.5. Mundus creatus est in tempore, seu cum tempore, non in tempore praeexsistente. Tempus enim mensura est motus creaturarum.
